items.stem: A skill works on the one example used to write it but fails on the next real case. What most likely went wrong?

options.text: The instructions hard-coded that example's details instead of generalising
options.rationale: Correct: reusable skills must generalise, not encode one case.
Length is not the core issue.
The issue is the instruction design, not capability.

items.stem: Which TWO belong in responsible skill testing? (Select TWO.)

options.rationale: Correct: multiple cases reveal failures a single test hides.

options.text: Finding and fixing failure cases before shipping
options.rationale: Correct: failures should be fixed, not ignored.
A single success does not establish reliability.
Fixes must be re-tested to confirm they work.

items.stem: Why review a skill before sharing it with a team?

options.text: To check what it instructs Claude to do and that it is safe
options.rationale: Correct: a shared skill runs for everyone, so its instructions must be reviewed.
Length is not the purpose of review.

options.text: To hide it from the team
options.rationale: The point is to share it safely, not hide it.
Review is about safety and quality, not speed.
